Slapstick and pathos can make for uneasy bedfellows, it is then perhaps a mark of the quality of Terry Johnson's 1992 play Dead Funny that they marry so well and provide the basis for an evening of wonderful and emotionally moving entertainment.

cn.t: Johnson's 1994 comedy-drama expertly blends slapstick humor with emotional depth. Critics praise the brilliant writing and superb cast, particularly Katherine Parkinson, for delivering both laughs and pathos in this emotionally moving revival.
